Examples: 
1. The probability that Arnel studies and passes his math test is 0.45. If the probability that he studies is 0.80, what is the probability that he passes the math test, given that he has studied? 
\Solution 
\quad Let B be the event that he studies, so P(B) = 0.80. P(A and B) = 0.45. 
\quad Using the formula. P(A | B) = \frac{P(A and B}{P(B)} = \frac{0.45}{0.80} = 0.5625 
2. One hundred students go to a leadership camp. After grouping, the number of boys and girls in each group are as follows: 
\begin{center} \begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline Group & Red & Blue & Green & Purple \\ \hline Boy & 14 & 18 & 15 & 13 \ \hline Girl & 11 & 7 & 10 & 12 \\ \hline \end{tabular} \end{center} 
If a student is chosen at random from these 100 students to give a self-introduction, find the probability that a student from the blue group is chosen, given that the student is a boy. 
\quad Solution: Looking at the table, the P(blue group and boy) = \frac{18}{100}, while P(boy) = \frac{60}{100}. Thus P(blue group given boy ) = \frac{\frac{18}{60}}{\frac{60}{100}} = \frac{18}{60} = \frac{3}{10}

3. 3. A fair die is thrown twice. Given that the first throw is an odd number, what is the probability that the sum of the numbers obtained is 7? 
\quad Solution: Let A be the event that the sum of the numbers obtained is 7 so A = {(1,6), (6,1), (2,5), (5,2), (3,4), (4,3)}, B be the event that the first throw is an odd number so B = {(1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (1,4), (1,5), (1,6), (3, 1),…, (5,1), (5,2), (5,3), (5,4), (5,5),(5,6)} and P(B) = \frac{18}{36}, . A and B = {(1,6), (5,2), (3,4)}, so P(A and B) = = \frac{3}{36}. 
\quad Substituting in the formula P(A | B) = \frac{P(A and B}{P(B)} = \frac{\frac{3}{36}}{\frac{18}{36}} = \frac{3}{18} = \frac{1}{6}.
